title: metadata-stewardship-auto-docgen-for-new-model-onboarding
creator: Asha Patel
description: Background: We continue to onboard a variety of open-source and vendor models (quantized variants, fused-kernel builds, tuned checkpoints). Current onboarding requires manual authoring of human-readable docs, inconsistent metadata fields, and ad-hoc provenance notes. This work creates a metadata stewardship pipeline that validates model manifests, generates consistent human-facing docs automatically from typed metadata, and stamps provenance + performance signatures for pinned variants. Goals: reduce reviewer effort, eliminate missing fields that cause runtime fallback surprises, and provide an auditable doc that SRE/Support/Customer Success can reference.
acceptance_criteria: A typed metadata schema (JSON Schema) is authored and validated against existing catalog entries with migration scripts
An automated doc generator writes a one-page model summary (README) from metadata and uploads to model-docs storage
Onboarding CI linter fails if required provenance/perf fields are missing (fingerprint, variant_id, baseline_throughput, baseline_latency_p50)
Pinning workflow requires a perf-signature artifact to be present before a variant can be marked 'stable'
Docs include a machine-readable 'compatibility' block for runtime heuristics (quantization flags, kernel hints, max_seq_length)
Security review checklist is produced for any private or gated model onboarding and the pipeline records reviewer name + timestamp
implementation_steps: Design JSON Schema for canonical metadata and publish it in /infra/catalog/schemas/model-metadata.json
Add schema-based validators to ingest pipeline (lambda + catalog-service) and migration tool to reconcile legacy entries
Implement docgen service: transform metadata -> markdown/HTML template, include perf signatures and provenance table
Hook docgen into CI: on model manifest merge, generate docs artifact and attach to catalog entry; fail merge if critical fields missing
Add pin gating: require perf-signature artifact and at least one smoke-test pass on dedicated shards before allowing 'stable' pin
Create an operator UI in Console to view generated docs and provenance stamps for audit purposes
Ship migration to convert 50% of existing catalog entries to new schema as a pilot, run smoke tests, then full migration
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Overly strict schema blocks valid community models. Mitigation: Allow opt-in compatibility flags and staged 'lenient' validation mode for initial pilot
Risk: Docgen template leaks internal runtime heuristics. Mitigation: Restrict template fields and sanitize kernel/hint strings; docs differ between internal-only and public modes
Risk: Migration could introduce regressions to serving. Mitigation: Pilot on low-traffic models, add canary rollout for catalog read path, and keep rollback playbook
testing_plan: Unit tests for schema validator with representative legacy manifests
Integration test: ingest -> docgen -> catalog attach -> Console view
Performance smoke tests for pinned variants (throughput and latency thresholds) executed in CI against dedicated test pool
Security checklist run by Security reviewer before enabling 'stable' pin on restricted models
rollout_and_observability: Phase 1: Schema + validator + docgen behind feature flag; run migration in dry-run mode and collect linter reports
Phase 2: Enable enforcement for new model merges only; surface linter failures to PR checks
Phase 3: Pilot migration for small model subset; monitor fallback rate and pin-change churn in Console dashboards
Observability: add catalog-lint metric, docgen-failure counter, and a dashboard showing number of models with complete perf signatures
notes: Design decision: prefer explicit fields (baseline_throughput, baseline_latency_p50) over heuristics inferred from CI runs to make rollbacks reproducible
We will include a short 'operational guidance' fragment in generated docs (how to reproduce perf test, flamegraph links) to help support triage
This ticket covers catalog-side changes and CI hooks; separate follow-ups will add Console editing and RBAC for doc visibility
